plan.title: AD lesional vs control: Hallmark pathway enrichment from DE results
plan.analytical_narrative: The de_results.csv already delivers the DESeq2 treated (AD lesional) vs control contrast for this skin dataset (12000 genes x 12 samples, 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch). The research question asks only which hallmark pathways are enriched — no new differential expression model is to be fit. Per the knowledge-service procedure for enrichment starting from a delivered results table (R-0110), the plan: (1) runs sample-structure QC on the raw counts to characterize sample_01's low library size (~4x below median) and confirm it does not distort the group structure, since removal is a judgment call and not automatic (R-0008/R-0030); (2) runs preranked GSEA (gseapy prerank, the fgsea-equivalent method the knowledge check validated) on the full ranked gene list ordered by the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat' column) against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection (2026.1, 50 sets) as the primary answer to the research question; (3) extends the same ranked-list method to Reactome and WikiPathways human collections as the follow-up context the knowledge service specifies after Hallmark (R-0098, R-0165), each pinned to its release; (4) assembles a report stating the contrast direction, the ranking metric, the collection versions, the gene-set size window, leading-edge genes per significant hallmark set, and the method-dependence caveat. All scripts are Python-only per the user's constraint; gseapy.prerank stands in for fgsea (both validated by the knowledge check as the permitted ranked-list method). No new DE model, no over-representation test (the delivered table's significant gene count has not been checked against the ~50-gene ORA floor, and a ranked test avoids that dependency entirely), and no translational/biomarker steps, because the question is bounded to pathway enrichment on an existing contrast.
